chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Ridha (peace be upon him) who said:
The owner of bounty is obligated to extend generously to his dependants.

key_terms.التَّوْسِعَةُ: Extending generously, providing with amplitude; not merely meeting minimum needs but ensuring comfort and ease
key_terms.صَاحِبُ النِّعْمَةِ: The owner/possessor of bounty — one who has been granted wealth or provision by God
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: His dependants — those whose maintenance is his legal and moral responsibility, including spouse, children, and others under his care

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the obligation of a wealthy person toward their family?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Ridha (peace be upon him) declares that one who has been blessed with wealth or resources has a religious obligation to provide generously for those under his care. This ruling comes from a chapter in al-Kafi dedicated to the duty of adequately providing for one's dependants, addressing the head of household who has means. The Imam's teaching reflects the Quranic principle that God's bounties entail social responsibilities, particularly toward one's family.
